note: Hand-derived from SecretsIAMAssumesIAMRoleEdgeUpsertCypher (go/internal/storage/cypher/cloud/aws/iam/secrets_graph_writer.go), NOT from the port or family name. The template is `MATCH (s:SecretsIAMServiceAccount {uid: row.service_account_uid}) MATCH (c:CloudResource {uid: row.cloud_resource_uid}) MERGE (s)-[rel:SECRETS_IAM_ASSUMES_IAM_ROLE]->(c)`, and the token is static in the template (no %s: no value is ever encoded into a relationship type). The relationship MERGEs on its two endpoint nodes alone, so there is no identity block. The template SETs rel.assume_mode as a bounded, offline-stable classification of the IAM-role evidence kind (web_identity for IRSA, pod_identity for EKS Pod Identity), so the offline edge carries it as properties. The CloudResource targets are the redaction-safe uids the trust chain resolves from each lane's aws_iam_principal scan boundary (account_id plus region) and role ARN -- the same uid the AWS resource projection commits for the lane's aws_resource fact. Exactly two edges: lane A resolves an IRSA web-identity exact chain (service account sa-assumes-app-a assuming role assumes-app-a), lane B an EKS Pod Identity exact chain (sa-assumes-app-b assuming role assumes-app-b). Lane A binds two Vault roles, so its chain resolves twice and both rows converge on the one edge -- the duplicate-delivery proof. The other four lanes contribute nothing on purpose -- lane C's IRSA annotation carries no web-identity subject for any trust to match (fingerprint-only), lane D's subject matches nothing its role's trust allows (partial chain), lane E's Deny trust statement grants nothing, and lane F's wildcard web-identity subject never matches exactly.
